newsitem.title: UK: MGAM chief says stands by Horlick action.
newsitem.headline: MGAM chief says stands by Horlick action.

text.p: The head of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, at the centre of a storm over the departure of star fund manager Nicola Horlick, said on Friday it stands by its actions and wants to develop its "great" business.
The assertion came in an internal memo to staff from chief executive Robert Smith, who earlier this week suspended Horlick.

"No one individual is bigger than the institution," Smith told his staff, having earlier made it clear that Horlick was suspended for allegedly attempting to move to a competitor firm with some of her colleagues.
"We are standing by our actions and we are completely satisfied that we have acted properly throughout," Smith said.

Horlick resigned on Thursday evening, accusing MGAM of "constructive dismissal" and on Friday travelled to Frankfurt in an attempt to put her case to the management board of MGAM's parent Deutsche Bank.

"MGAM is a great business. I have received whole-hearted support for the management team in dealing with this matter. We look forward to continuing the development of the business in 1997 and beyond," Smith said, adding that the superior performance of MGAM in recent years was the result of a concerted team effort.
